title: Cleanup and race prevention

publication.changeSummary: Technology-specific React: Component-Based Browser Applications draft for Cleanup and race prevention; independent standards, browser, pedagogy, and accessibility review required. Beginner-quality contract 1.0.0 applied deterministically from existing source-linked draft facts; publication stage and reviewer state are unchanged.

sources.locator: React Learn and Reference; React 19.2; provisions applicable to Cleanup and race prevention
sources.claim: An effect may return cleanup that reverses its subscription, timer, request, or connection before rerun and unmount.

canonicalExplanation.summary: An effect can **return a cleanup function** that undoes its setup: remove the listener, clear the timer, close the connection, abort the request. React runs cleanup **before the effect runs again** (when dependencies change) and when the component **unmounts**. Setup and cleanup should be **symmetric**: whatever you add, remove the same thing, and for listeners that means **the same function reference**. For fetches, cleanup should abort or ignore the old request so a slow, outdated response can't overwrite newer data. StrictMode runs setup, cleanup, setup once in development to check this.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A lesson layout tracks the window width with `window.addEventListener("resize", () => setWidth(window.innerWidth))`. After opening a few lessons, resizing becomes sluggish: dozens of listeners are still attached, some to components that no longer exist. A resize listener is removed with the exact same function reference when the effect cleans up. In this lesson you'll implement and test setup-cleanup symmetry and latest-request behavior.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know the **State and events** module, the **Promises, async work and HTTP** module, **Dependencies and reactive values**, and **Cancellation, timeout and stale results** (AbortController).

sections.heading: The model: every setup has a matching cleanup
StrictMode's check

includes: Return cleanup that exactly reverses listeners, timers, connections and requests.
Prevent outdated responses from overwriting newer data.

outcomes: Implement and test setup-cleanup symmetry and latest-request behavior.

examples.title: The resize listener that piled up
examples.situation: A resize listener is removed with the exact same function reference when the effect cleans up.
walkthrough: **Bug:** the effect added an arrow listener and returned no cleanup, so each mount left one behind.
**Same function reference:** onResize is defined once in the effect, added in setup and removed in cleanup.
**Test:** a test will mount and unmount the component, then fire a resize event and assert setWidth isn't called for the unmounted one.
examples.result: Only mounted components listen to resize, and resizing stays smooth however many lessons are opened.

examples.title: The lesson title that flickered back
examples.situation: Clicking lesson 1 then quickly lesson 2 sometimes shows lesson 2, then switches to lesson 1's title when its slow response arrives.
walkthrough: Both fetches were running; the older one finished last.
Nothing stopped the outdated response from calling setLesson.
Fix: create an AbortController per run and abort it in cleanup, ignoring AbortError.
examples.result: The page always shows the most recently chosen lesson.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: Cleanup runs only when the whole application closes, not before an effect reruns.
misconceptions.correction: React runs cleanup before every re-run of the effect (when dependencies change) and when the component unmounts. That's what keeps one listener, one connection and one current request.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The lesson title that flickered back", when should the first request have been aborted?

analogy.example: Setup and cleanup are like **checking into and out of a hotel room**. Before moving to a new room (a dependency change) or leaving the hotel (unmount), you check out: return the key you were given, not a copy you made (same reference).
limitations: Hotels charge for forgotten checkouts; apps pay with leaks and slow pages.
StrictMode is a practice check-in and check-out on day one.

steps.explanation: The effect adds the resize listener.
The resize listener is removed with the exact same function reference.
Events after unmount reach nothing, so no leak remains.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing setup and cleanup. Step 1, Setup: listeners is 1 (onResize). The effect adds the resize listener. Step 2, Cleanup: removed is onResize; listeners is 0. The resize listener is removed with the exact same function reference. Step 3, After: setWidth calls is 0. Events after unmount reach nothing, so no leak remains.

nearTransfer.prompt: Write `useInterval(callback, ms)` that sets an interval and clears it in cleanup, re-creating it when ms changes. Test that unmounting stops the callback.
expectedEvidence: No calls after unmount (use fake timers).

farTransfer.prompt: Build a lesson search that fetches on each query change with abort in cleanup. Write a test with controlled fake responses that resolve out of order, and prove only the latest results render.

remediation.explanation: For each effect, write two columns: **what setup adds** and **what cleanup removes**. Every line on the left needs a matching line on the right, with the same reference or id.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The lesson title that flickered back".

recap.summary: To implement setup-cleanup symmetry and latest-request behavior, return a cleanup from each effect that removes the same listener reference, clears timers, closes connections and aborts requests. React runs it before each re-run and on unmount, so outdated work can't leak or overwrite newer data.
